method.selection_policy: LLM-selected market-relevant items from news_digest.json; preserves source metadata and excludes noise.

framework.Equities: Broad equity/risk sentiment; market-moving mega-cap/AI allowed; low-signal single-stock noise excluded.
framework.Commodities: Physical commodity futures framework; supply disruption/demand strength positive; supply increase/demand weakness negative.
framework.FX: USD-centric basket; non-USD currency strength positive; USD/DXY strength negative.
framework.Rates: Bond-price framework; yields up/selloff/higher-for-longer negative; yields down/bond rally/cooler inflation positive.

Equities.title: Equities: Risk-on rotation with Iran peace hopes – Danske Bank
Equities.summary: Danske Research Team reports a strong risk-on session in equities, driven by optimism around a possible US–Iran deal and lower Oil prices. Cyclical growth and momentum outperformed, while defensives and energy lagged.
Equities.reason: Clear risk-on move tied to improving geopolitical outlook and falling oil — broad positive for equities/risk assets. Relevance high because it reflects market-wide sentiment and commodity-driven impact on cyclicals.

Equities.reason: Mega-cap Nvidia delivered strong revenue/forecasts but the stock reaction was muted/dip — mixed signal. Still positive for long-term AI-led demand, but near-term market reaction reduces upside for broad indices.

Equities.reason: Large move in a major conglomerate tied to AI/IPO momentum supports risk appetite and tech sector flows. Relevance moderate-high given SoftBank's market footprint and signalling effect for AI-related listings.

Equities.reason: OpenAI IPO prospects reinforce AI sector momentum and could draw significant capital into tech equities; positive for risk appetite though timing/details uncertain.

Rates.summary: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee, April 28-29, 2026

Rates.reason: Reuters reports bond yields falling on hopes of an Iran deal — yields down (bond rally) as geopolitical risk premium eases; positive for bonds but story is event-driven and regionally focused.

Rates.title: Gilts Jump as UK Inflation Surprise Curbs Rate-Hike Wagers
Rates.reason: UK inflation surprise that reduces rate-hike expectations leads to gilt rally (yields lower) — positive for UK bonds and relevant for global rate sentiment given Gilt market importance.

Rates.title: Japan’s Super-Long Bonds See First Foreign Outflow Since 2024
Rates.reason: Foreign outflows from super-long JGBs imply selling pressure and higher yields in the long end of the Japanese curve; notable for JGB market dynamics and cross-border flows.

Rates.title: South Korea Set to Reduce Debt Sales in June as Bonds Slump
Rates.reason: Reports of Korean authorities cutting planned issuance amid a bond slump signal market stress and tighter supply management; negative for local bond sentiment and relevant for Asian rates.

Rates.title: Australia Jobless Rate Jumps to 4-1/2 Year High as RBA Bets Fade
Rates.reason: A jump in Australian unemployment weakens the case for further RBA tightening, which should be positive for Australian bonds (lower yields) and eases local rate-hike pricing.

Rates.reason: A 50bp BI hike is directly hawkish for Indonesian rates (higher policy rates) and supports regional EM rate repricing; relevant for EM fixed income flows.

Rates.title: India Weighs Measures Including Rate Hike to Stabilize Rupee
Rates.reason: India considering rate hikes to defend the rupee points to potential tightening and higher local rates — negative for bond prices in India and relevant for EM rate outlook.

FX.title: ECB’s Rehn: Raising rates may be needed in adverse scenario to maintain credibility
FX.summary: European Central Bank (ECB) official and Finnish Central Bank Governor Olli Rehn said that under adverse circumstances, it might be necessary to raise interest rates to maintain credibility, Reuters reported on Thursday.
FX.reason: ECB official signaling potential further hikes is bullish for the euro vs the dollar (reduces relative USD safe-haven), a meaningful central-bank comment with clear FX implications.

FX.reason: Cooling UK inflation is dovish for sterling while geopolitical risk keeps USD demand; net effect is mild GBP weakness vs USD.

FX.title: US Dollar Index hovers around 99.00 due to US-Iran peace hopes
FX.summary: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, is remaining steady after registering modest losses in the previous day and hovering around 99.10 during the Asian hours on Thursday.
FX.reason: DXY steadiness amid peace hopes suggests a slight easing of safe-haven USD demand — modestly positive for other currencies, limited directional impact.

FX.title: WTI edges lower below $98.50 on US-Iran deal optimism
FX.summary: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the US crude oil benchmark, is trading around $98.20 during the early European trading hours on Thursday. The WTI price edges lower after US President Donald Trump said talks with Iran are in the final stages.
FX.reason: Oil easing on deal optimism lowers risk-premium and inflationary pressure — generally positive for oil-importing currencies and risk-sensitive FX; relevance moderate.

FX.title: Germany’s flash Manufacturing PMI unexpectedly declines to 49.9 vs. 51.0 estimates
FX.summary: German flash HCOB Composite PMI improves to 48.6 in May, while it was expected to remain steady at 48.4. However, a figure below 50.0 is considered a contraction in the overall business activity.
FX.reason: Soft German PMI is negative for euro-area growth outlook and thus negative for EUR vs USD; important euro-area macro datapoint.

FX.title: New Zealand Dollar weakens despite stronger Trade Balance data
